info.title: Paiflow API v1
info.description:
Execute a deployed deposit-triggered flow (Pay, Split, condition, swap) and poll its on-chain events from your own backend.

Every `/api/v1/deployments/{id}/…` call authenticates with a deployment API token (`Authorization: Bearer pfk_…`) that the deployment's owner mints in the **API access** panel on the deployment page. A token reaches exactly one deployment.

**Execute deposits are signed by the caller.** `execute` returns an unsigned envelope; you sign it with the `from` key, which stays on your side, and post it to `execute/submit`. A leaked token can prepare and relay a deposit you signed. Webhook and early-release operations use the relayer.

Successful responses are `{ "data": … }`. Errors are `{ "error": { code, message, fields?, details? } }`:

| Code | HTTP status |
| --- | --- |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 |
| `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | 402 |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| `VALIDATION` | 422 |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 |
| `INTERNAL` | 500 |
| `UPSTREAM_RPC` | 502 |

Rate limits are per token and per endpoint (each operation lists its own). A token that has been issued or has worked in the last 30 days is subject to nothing else. Any other token is limited per client address before it is looked up: 6000 lookups per 60 seconds, and, after 300 failed authentications in 600 seconds from the address, 60 per 60 seconds. A token refused in the last minute is refused again without a lookup. So one caller's bad token does not lock out others on the same network.

No account? `POST /api/v1/demo-token` hands you a short-lived token for a shared demo flow, so every call above can be tried straight away.

The public instance runs on Stellar **testnet**. Guide: `docs/api/README.md`.

get.summary: Discover a deployment's supported integration paths
get.description:
Supported means the integration path exists for the recorded deployment. Conditional requires additional eligibility checks. Unsupported means no matching path can be established. No status guarantees current balances, configuration, consent, deadline or infrastructure readiness.

Requires this deployment's pfk_ bearer token and a confirmed deployment on the environment's network. Reads only recorded deployment metadata: no RPC, simulation, transaction submission or mutation. inputAsset is initial snapshot metadata and may be stale after Dev mutations; null means unavailable. The recorded pipeline determines contract kinds, not the current editable flow.

Operations are execute (execute and execute/submit), events, transactions, releaseEarly (release-early), payouts (payouts and payouts/submit), webhook (/api/webhooks/{id}), and subscriptionAllowance (/api/deployments/{id}/subscription-allowance and its submit/status paths, or /allowance/{id}). Each includes status, authentication, requirements and candidate nodeIds. Conditional payouts and subscription approval must be checked by their own preparation/state endpoints; discovery does not establish live eligibility. nodeIds are candidates, not a guarantee that a chosen amount or path succeeds. A webhook_secret or subscriber_wallet operation is not authorized by the discovery token.

Returns an explicit projection without webhook secrets, API credentials, recipients, subscriber addresses, bank details, KYC, notification settings or private graph configuration. Responses are no-store.

Rate limit: 60 requests per 60 seconds per token.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Deployment id (UUID). A malformed id is a 404.

200.description: Deployment integration support and prerequisites, not live readiness.

requirements: The paying wallet signs the prepared deposit; simulation checks current configuration.
Recorded events can lag the chain.
Only attributable transactions can be read; missing evidence does not prove failure.
No deployed timelock branch supports early release.
Standard flows use configured recipients; per-payment recipients require an eligible Dev flow.
Requires a deployed webhook trigger with HTTP callbacks enabled.

post.summary: Release a webhook flow, with optional durable event idempotency
post.description: Authenticate with x-webhook-secret, not pfk_. Deposit funding separately. For pre-funded release use escrow:true and a stroop amount; omitted amount or zero releases the whole available pool. Idempotency-Key is optional: matching requests return the original attempt without another send; different effective arguments return 409. Keys are deployment-scoped, never automatically expire, and store only key/request digests. One hash is persisted before sending; keyed sends never rebuild/resubmit automatically. Interrupted preparation without a hash remains UNKNOWN and requires operator review. Unknown/missing RPC evidence never authorizes another payment. Use the same key to poll and a pfk_ token for the transaction lookup endpoint. Unkeyed requests retain legacy behavior and can each release another payout. Fixed recipients with Dev mode off. Rate limit: 20/minute per deployment/client IP; keyed replays additionally share transaction lookup RPC limits.

post.summary: Prepare a deposit with a per-payment recipient
post.description:
Configure one immediate dev Pay for this recipient, then prepare its deposit.

Requires a confirmed deposit-triggered dev flow and one selected PAYER_DEV. Only immediate paths through amount conditions and fixed Split are supported. Current on-chain connectivity and values are checked against the deployed graph. Split must have zero token and accumulated balances, a fixed crypto roster and a deposit greater than its total; it forwards the surplus immediately and resets its accumulator. Percentage Split, shortfalls, delayed/unsupported paths and deposits that miss this Pay are refused.

For fillValueViaApi, Pay is set to 100%. Otherwise its current configured value is preserved: percentage must consume all incoming funds, or fixed incoming funds must be at most its fixed cap (Pay pays min(incoming, cap)). Pay must start with zero balance. Recipient account/trustline checks must succeed before mutation; unchanged configuration skips the relayer transaction.

Requires functioning Redis. Concurrent preparation returns CONFLICT. Coordination records retain uncertain configuration transactions and the exact prepared deposit through finality or ledger-time expiry; wall-clock expiry does not release protection. Payout deposits have a 60-second validity window; execute retains 180 seconds. Sign this xdr before expiresAt and post it to payouts/submit using the same token. Direct deposits, execute, legacy dev mutations and owner transactions bypass this coordination. Never flush payout coordination records while transactions may still land.

Rate limit: 10 requests per 60 seconds per token.

post.description:
Submit exactly the transaction prepared by payouts for this token and deployment, with envelope signatures added.

The hash must match the exact prepared deposit for this deployment and API token. Changing amount, source, operations, bounds or authorization entries is refused; add envelope signatures only. Fee-bump envelopes are refused. PENDING or uncertain RPC outcomes retain recipient protection. Confirmed finality releases only this holder, never a newer payout's protection. A network submission refusal can return FAILED while protection remains until finality or ledger-time expiry. Retry the same signedXdr to obtain status; final retries remain available for seven days. An expired unconfirmed envelope cannot be resubmitted after a successor acquires protection.

Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds per token.

post.summary: Prepare the unsigned deposit that executes a deposit-triggered flow
post.description:
Prepare the deposit that executes a deposit-triggered flow. `from` must be a funded account on this network: it pays the deposit and the fee, and signs the envelope. For issued assets, the sender and payout recipients must hold trustlines for the assets they transfer; a missing trustline reverts the whole pipeline.

The flow runs through its deposit trigger; the next pipeline steps (pay, split, condition, swap) run as part of the same transaction. Sign the returned `xdr` with the `from` key using `networkPassphrase`, before `expiresAt`, and post it to `execute/submit`. Only flows that start with a deposit trigger can be executed; subscription, webhook, payroll and other trigger-headed flows are refused with `VALIDATION`. A Pay or Split step with no recipient yet (dev mode) reverts with a plain message.

Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds per token.

post.summary: Submit the signed deposit and wait for the result
post.description:
Submit a signed deposit that executes a deposit-triggered flow.

The envelope must be the one `execute` returned, signed by `from`: anything but a single `deposit` call on this flow's trigger contract is refused with `VALIDATION`, as is a fee-bump envelope.

Idempotent on the envelope hash: submitting the same `signedXdr` again never sends a second transaction, it reports the one already on the network. That is also how to check a `PENDING` result. A transaction that reached the network and failed is a `200` with `status: FAILED` and an `error`, not an HTTP error.

Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds per token.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Deployment id (UUID). A malformed id is a 404.

parameters.name: x-preparation-request-id
parameters.description: The preparation response's x-history-request-id. Send it with this prepared envelope and reuse it on retries; a new preparation gets a new ID. Optional analytics correlation only: it does not authorize or deduplicate a payment. Reports verify the account, token, deployment, operation and context before linking requests.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: `false` returns PENDING as soon as the network accepts the transaction. Default `true`: wait up to about 25 seconds for a final status, then return `PENDING` if there is none yet. At most 3 calls per token wait at once; a call over that still sends the transaction and returns `PENDING` straight away, as `wait=false` does. Resubmit the same `signedXdr` to check it.

post.summary: Release a timelock branch's before side now
post.description:
Release a timelock branch's before side now (work delivered), ahead of its deadline.

For a flow like 'pay on delivery, refund the client after the deadline': call this when the work is delivered and the relayer pays the before side. Nothing is signed on your side; the token is the authorisation. Unlike `execute`, this sends a transaction and returns once it is final.

After the deadline the contract refuses the before side and this returns `VALIDATION` (422): the condition then releases to its after side automatically. It also returns `VALIDATION` when the condition holds no funds, or when the deployment has several timelock branches and `nodeId` is missing or unknown. The body may be omitted when there is exactly one branch.

Rate limit: 10 requests per 60 seconds per token.

get.summary: Look up an attributed transaction without resubmitting
get.description: Accepts this deployment's pfk_ token. SUCCESS and FAILED are final; REJECTED means submission refusal, not on-chain failure. PENDING requires known acceptance. UNKNOWN means an attributed attempt has no established acceptance or finality; it never authorizes a new payment. Unattributed hashes return 404, including missing outside submissions. Supports execute records, queued webhook audit records, early-release audit records, ingested events and verified direct pipeline invocations in recent RPC envelopes. Outside indirect calls and token transfers alone are unsupported. Stored terminal outcomes and ingested events survive RPC retention; missing historical evidence cannot be reconstructed. Poll after 2 seconds, exponentially back off with jitter to 30 seconds; honor Retry-After on 429. RPC failures return 502, never FAILED. One bounded RPC read per request, at most 60/min per deployment across tokens; production requires shared Redis for that RPC budget. Rate limit: 60 requests per 60 seconds per token across transaction hashes.

get.summary: Poll the deployment's events, oldest first
get.description:
Forward-paginated events the app decoded for this deployment's contracts, ascending by `(ledger, eventId)`. This is the app's record, not a raw chain feed: each event appears once (`eventId` is unique).

**Freshness.** When this deployment's events were last collected from the network more than 10 seconds ago, a call collects them first and waits up to 5 seconds for that before answering from the record. So an event usually appears within 10 to 20 seconds of its ledger closing, whoever submitted the transaction (a wallet paying the contract directly, a scanned SEP-7 QR, a scheduled charge), provided you keep polling. Collection is shared by every caller of the deployment: one at a time, and the next no sooner than 10 seconds after the last one ends, so polling faster than that does not make events arrive sooner. A call that arrives while a collection is already running, or when the network is slow, answers with what is recorded, and the event appears on a later call; a background poller also collects every minute. A confirmed `execute/submit` records its own events before it returns.

A swap is `kind: PAYOUT` with `topic: "swap"` and `data` `{ assetIn, assetOut, amountIn, amountOut }`; amounts are stroops as strings.

To poll: store `nextCursor` and pass it back as `cursor`. While `hasMore` is true, ask again straight away; once it is false, wait and ask again with the same cursor. `nextCursor` is never null once the deployment has events: on an empty page it echoes the cursor you sent. It is null only when there are no events and no cursor was sent.

Rate limit: 120 requests per 60 seconds per token.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`. Omit to start from the first event. An empty or altered value is a 422.

parameters.description: Only events from this transaction, e.g. the `txHash` `execute/submit` returned.

post.summary: Get a short-lived token for the public demo deployment
post.description:
Public; no token and no account. Returns a bearer token for one shared swapper deployment on testnet, so you can run the calls above before registering. Takes no body. Available only where the public demo is enabled (the testnet instance); 403 otherwise.

**This deployment is shared.** Anyone else holding a demo token can read the events your deposit produces, including the account you deposited from. The swap proceeds are paid to a Paiflow-owned testnet account, not back to you, so the testnet XLM you deposit is spent. Fund a throwaway account with friendbot and never point this at an account you care about.

For an isolated deployment and a token that does not expire in an hour, register, deploy your own flow and mint a token in the **API access** panel.

Rate limit: 3 requests per 3600 seconds per client IP. Rate limit: 60 requests per 3600 seconds instance-wide.

403.description: `FORBIDDEN`: The public demo is not enabled on this instance.

429.description: `RATE_LIMITED`: Too many demo tokens from this address, or the instance is at its hourly cap.

500.description: `INTERNAL`: The demo deployment is not configured, confirmed or deposit-triggered. One message for every case; the operator is alerted.

txHash.description: Hash of the confirmed release transaction, hex.

ledger.description: Ledger the transaction was final in.

topic.description: The event's first topic: `swap` for a swap, whose `kind` is `PAYOUT`.

data.description: The decoded event body; `null` when the app does not decode it.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor`. Null only when the deployment has no events and no cursor was sent.

hasMore.description: True when another page is ready now.

DemoToken.description: A short-lived token for the shared demo deployment on testnet.

deploymentId.description: The shared demo deployment this token reaches, and the only one it reaches.

token.description: Bearer token for the routes above. Shown once and never retrievable again.

expiresAt.description: ISO time the token stops working. Ask again for a new one.
